newsitem.title: USA: Stop & Shop settles U.S. fraud claims.
newsitem.headline: Stop & Shop settles U.S. fraud claims.

text.p: Stop & Shop Cos Inc has agreed to pay the United States $700,000 to settle civil claims arising out of allegedly fraudulent promotional practices, U.S. Attorney Donald K. Stern said Friday
In return, Stop & Shop said in a separate statement, the U.S. Attorney will release all claims against Stop & Shop and its officers, directors and employees.
The parties agreed to settle the disputed claims to avoid the uncertainty and expense of further litigation, the company said.

The government said its claims were based on the Mail Fraud Injunction Statute, and arise out of two promotional practices that relate to the method by which Stop & Shop obtained reimbursement from food vendors for goods sold at "sale" prices. Stop & Shop has discontinued both non-disclosure practices, the government statement said.

In one practice, called a "scan bill back," Stop & Shop did not disclose that the invoices it sent vendors inflated by 20 percent the amount of merchandise recorded by Stop & Shop's electronic scanners during a sale, the government said.
Stop & Shop did not disclose this 20 percent inflation factor to vendors, although the company contends its scan data were unreliable and grossly understated the actual amount of product sold.

In the second practice, called a "temporary price reduction," Stop & Shop did not disclose that the invoices it sent vendors were based on sales figures from all Stop & Shop stores, even though the sale prices had not been implemented in stores located in what Stop & Shop calls "Shaw's Zones," the government said.
The government said these are areas where Stop & Shop competes with Shaw's grocery stores.
